samf-junior-2000-r1-02.title: Compare volumes
samf-junior-2000-r1-02.body:
Box A: $10\times4\times6=240\text{ cm}^3$. Box B: $2\times5\times1=10\text{ cm}^3$. $240\div10=24$ boxes. (They do fit: Box B's 2, 5, 1 cm sides divide 10, 4 ... e.g. arrange the 5 cm side along the 10 cm side and 1 cm along 4 cm, and 2 cm along 6 cm: $2\times4\times3=24$.)

**Answer: (A) 24**

samf-junior-2000-r1-03.title: Pascal's triangle
samf-junior-2000-r1-03.body:
Each number is the sum of the two above it (Pascal's triangle). The last row is $1,6,15,20,15,6,1$, and the square is $10+10=20$ (or: the row above is $1,5,10,10,5,1$).

**Answer: (B) 20**

samf-junior-2000-r1-04.title: Angles on straight lines
samf-junior-2000-r1-04.body:
$\angle CBD=180^\circ-110^\circ=70^\circ$ and $\angle CDB=180^\circ-130^\circ=50^\circ$. In triangle BCD: $\hat C=180^\circ-70^\circ-50^\circ=60^\circ$.

**Answer: (D) $60^\circ$**

samf-junior-2000-r1-04.title: Exterior angle
samf-junior-2000-r1-04.body:
$\angle EDB=130^\circ$ is exterior to triangle BCD, so equals $\hat C+\angle CBD=\hat C+70^\circ$. Thus $\hat C=60^\circ$.

**Answer: (D) $60^\circ$**

samf-junior-2000-r1-08.title: Relative speed
samf-junior-2000-r1-08.body:
The minute hand gains $360-30=330^\circ$ per hour on the hour hand, i.e. $5.5^\circ$ per minute. They form a right angle whenever the gap is $90^\circ+180^\circ k$. After 12:00 this happens at $t=\frac{90+180k}{5.5}$ minutes. For $360\le t\le720$ we need $1980\le90+180k\le3960$, i.e. $k=11,12,\dots,21$: 11 times.

**Answer: (B) 11**

samf-junior-2000-r1-08.title: List the times
samf-junior-2000-r1-08.body:
Using the same formula, the right angles occur at about 6:16, 6:49, 7:22, 7:55, 8:27, 9:00, 9:33, 10:05, 10:38, 11:11 and 11:44. That is 11 times.

**Answer: (B) 11**

samf-junior-2000-r1-09.title: Totals
samf-junior-2000-r1-09.body:
The original total was $3\times18=54$ and the new total is $3\times23=69$. The total went up by 15, so the new number 38 is 15 more than the original one: $38-15=23$.

**Answer: (B) 23**

samf-junior-2000-r1-10.title: Row sums are cubes
samf-junior-2000-r1-10.body:
Row 1: $1$. Row 2: $3+5=8$. Row 3: $7+9+11=27$. Row 4: $13+15+17+19=64$. The row sums are $1^3,2^3,3^3,4^3$. (The row $n$ has $n$ odd numbers with middle value $n^2$, so the sum is $n\cdot n^2$.) For $n=100$: $100^3=1\,000\,000$.

**Answer: (A) 1 000 000**

samf-junior-2000-r1-11.title: Unit fraction
samf-junior-2000-r1-11.body:
$\frac45$ takes 8 hours so $\frac15$ takes 2 hours. The remainder is $\frac15$ of the container: 2 hours.

**Answer: (C) 2**

samf-junior-2000-r1-12.title: Lowest common multiple
samf-junior-2000-r1-12.body:
One lap is 12 cm and the other 18 cm. The ants walk equal distances, and are together again at $A$ only when both have completed whole laps: the least common multiple $\operatorname{lcm}(12,18)=36$ cm. (They cannot meet earlier: they share only the point A.)

**Answer: (D) 36**

samf-junior-2000-r1-13.title: Total of all nine
samf-junior-2000-r1-13.body:
Adding the last column: $A+\dots+I=20+14+12=46$. The first column adds to 17, so $P+Q=46-17=29$.

**Answer: (A) 29**

samf-junior-2000-r1-14.title: Arrangements
samf-junior-2000-r1-14.body:
The bottom cube can be chosen in 4 ways, the next in 3, then 2, then 1: $4\times3\times2\times1=24$.

**Answer: (D) 24**

samf-junior-2000-r1-15.title: Inclusion-exclusion
samf-junior-2000-r1-15.body:
Multiples of 2: 50; of 3: 33; of 6: 16. Removed: $50+33-16=67$. Remaining: $100-67=33$.

**Answer: (B) 33**

samf-junior-2000-r1-15.title: By blocks of 6
samf-junior-2000-r1-15.body:
In each block of six consecutive numbers $6k+1,\dots,6k+6$ only $6k+1$ and $6k+5$ survive. The numbers 1 to 96 give $16\times2=32$, and from 97 to 100 only 97 survives (98 and 100 are even, 99 is a multiple of 3): $32+1=33$.

**Answer: (B) 33**

samf-junior-2000-r1-16.title: Inscribed angle
samf-junior-2000-r1-16.body:
The angle $x$ at the vertex is an inscribed angle that subtends the arc between the two other end points of the chords, which consists of 2 sides of the octagon. Each side subtends $\frac{360^\circ}{8}=45^\circ$ at the centre, so the arc is $90^\circ$ and $x=\frac{90^\circ}{2}=45^\circ$.

**Answer: (C) 45**

samf-junior-2000-r1-17.title: Use the dimensions
samf-junior-2000-r1-17.body:
Let $AB=l$ and $BC=w$. Then $AE=\frac l2$ and the height from F to AB is $BF=\frac w2$, so the area of $\triangle AEF=\frac12\cdot\frac l2\cdot\frac w2=\frac{lw}8=7$ and $lw=56$.

**Answer: (E) 56**

samf-junior-2000-r1-18.title: Equations
samf-junior-2000-r1-18.body:
Let ruler $r$, pencil $p$, eraser $e$ (rand). $3r+p=2e$ and $r+2p+3e=25$. From the first, $p=2e-3r$; so $r+4e-6r+3e=25$, i.e. $7e-5r=25$ and $p=2e-3r>0$. Then $7e=25+5r$, so $r\equiv2\pmod 7$; $p>0$ forces $r\le4$, so $r=2$, $e=5$, $p=4$. Check: $6+4=10=2\times5$ and $2+8+15=25$.

**Answer: (D) R5**

samf-junior-2000-r1-20.title: Sum of odd numbers
samf-junior-2000-r1-20.body:
The sum of the first $n$ odd numbers is $n^2$. So $n^2=2304$; $48^2=2304$, so $n=48$.

**Answer: (D) 48**
